categories.CLOSED: Settled with fresh, falsifiable proof. Do not re-litigate without new evidence.
categories.PRODUCTIVE_FRONTIER: Actively worked, converts RAW_UNKNOWN into classified/matching bytes. This is where effort should go.

frontiers.matches: tools/lzexe_unpack.py produces build/DAVE_unpacked.exe (172848 bytes, MD5 86feba8cc84fc1f0d829fd731f6dbe20, SHA1 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13), independently cross-checked against a third-party-published UNLZEXE-decompressed DAVE.EXE with the same SHA1.

Borland Turbo C++ 1.00 (May 1990), confirmed two independent ways: (1) a 'Turbo C++ - Copyright 1990 Borland Intl.' runtime string embedded in build/DAVE_unpacked.exe, (2) the pinned TCC.EXE's own OMF self-identification string 'TC86 Borland Turbo C++ 1.00' when compiling a probe. Toolchain installed under toolchain/, pinned by SHA-256 in layout/toolchain.json.

Small model (-ms). Comparing the game's C startup code against all 5 Turbo C++ 1.00 memory-model startup objects, C0S.OBJ (small) is the unique model where every byte differing from the raw library object is explained by a linker fixup, with zero unexplained differences.

-N (checking ON). The real _main @ file offset 0x439 opens with 55 8B EC 39 26 9A 00 72 03 E8 (push bp; mov bp,sp; cmp [stackbase],sp; jb +3; call <handler>) with zero locals. Compiling tests/fixtures/probe2.c under -ms -N reproduces the identical push-bp/mov-bp,sp/cmp/jb/call structure (differing only by an inserted 'sub sp,N' for probe2's own locals, which _main lacks). Compiling with -N- omits the check triplet entirely, ruling it out.

layout/manifest.json owns all 172848 bytes of build/DAVE_unpacked.exe, no gaps/overlaps, verified by tools/reconstruct.py to rebuild an exact MD5 match. Now includes a KNOWN_LIBRARY region (STARTUP_C0S, 569 bytes) alongside MZ_HEADER/RELOCATION_TABLE/HEADER_PADDING/RAW_UNKNOWN.

File offset [0x200,0x439) is unmodified Turbo C++ 1.00 C0S.OBJ (small-model C startup), promoted from RAW_UNKNOWN to KNOWN_LIBRARY in layout/manifest.json. This also fixed the earlier _main coordinate bug: C0S's self-relative CALL fixup (opcode at file offset 0x2FC, disp16 0x013A) resolves via tools/coordinates.py to file offset 0x439 (load-module offset 0x239) -- NOT 0x639, which was a stale result from adding the 0x200 MZ-header size a second time to an already-file-relative value. tools/coordinates.py now centralizes this conversion and tests/test_coordinates.py regression-tests the exact numbers so this class of bug cannot silently reappear.

tools/function_census.py (now using tools/coordinates.py, asserts RAW_LOAD_MODULE_START == 0x439) scans for '55 8B EC' prologues and walks to RET/RETF, finding 193 candidate functions spanning file offset 0x439-0xB483 (~45KB), zero overlaps/truncations. No prologue matches occur past ~0xB483, suggesting _TEXT ends there and _DATA/_BSS follows (unproven -- see below).
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: The census is a naive prologue scan, not a call-graph traversal from the trusted _main root as docs/matching-phase.md now requires. It will miss frameless/leaf functions and cannot yet distinguish real functions from coincidental byte patterns in data.
frontiers.unblock: Rebuild the census as a conservative call-graph walk starting from _main @ 0x439: follow direct near CALL targets recursively, use RET boundaries and known prologue/library signatures, and cross-reference against external RE addresses (see 'Import yo-yo-yo-jbo RE facts' below) rather than relying on linear/pattern scanning alone.
frontiers.leverage: Every function pulled out of RAW_UNKNOWN via a verified boundary is progress; this is the main lever for reducing the ~99% RAW_UNKNOWN figure.

frontiers.target: Confirm _TEXT/_DATA segment boundary near file offset 0xB483
frontiers.matches: Absence of prologue-shaped bytes past ~0xB483 in the naive census is circumstantial evidence only.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: Not proven; could hide frameless code or hand-written ASM that a prologue scan cannot see.
frontiers.unblock: Cross-reference every CALL/JMP target found in the 0x439-0xB483 region against this boundary; look for positive evidence of _DATA (ASCII strings, structured tables) starting near 0xB483 rather than relying only on absence-of-code.
frontiers.leverage: Converts an inferred code/data split into a confirmed one, unblocking the data/asset census track for the tail of RAW_LOAD_MODULE.

frontiers.target: Import and verify yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave RE facts
frontiers.matches: https://github.com/yo-yo-yo-jbo/dangerous_dave analyzes an unpacked DAVE.EXE with SHA1 9e572f0320ca759bea8f24a0ebcfcb1b68474e13 -- identical to build/DAVE_unpacked.exe. Its function/data facts (level loading, warp-zone logic, game init, score/lives, level arrays, etc.) refer to the exact same bytes we have and can be mechanically verified rather than rediscovered.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: No addresses have been imported or cross-checked yet.
frontiers.unblock: For each address/fact the external project documents, independently verify against our bytes/xrefs (do not accept the name/semantics as truth) before recording it as a provenance-tagged hint in a new docs/external-re-evidence.json.
frontiers.leverage: Avoids re-deriving semantics the external project already worked out; accelerates the function census and matching-C candidate selection significantly.

frontiers.target: Scan Turbo C++ 1.00 libraries for additional exact library contributions
frontiers.matches: The same fixup-modulo-exact-match technique that identified STARTUP_C0S (tools/recover_startup_binding.py) should generalize to other unchanged runtime routines (memory/string/arithmetic/I/O helpers, exit routines, the stack-check handler itself) linked in from CC.LIB/CS.LIB's constituent modules.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: No systematic scan has been run yet; only the single C0S.OBJ startup module has been checked.
frontiers.unblock: Build a generalized library matcher: split CS.LIB into its member OMF modules (tools/omf.py already has split_library-equivalent capability to extend), and for each RAW_UNKNOWN byte range in layout/manifest.json, test whether any library module matches modulo fixups the same way STARTUP_C0S did.
frontiers.leverage: Potentially removes substantial RAW_UNKNOWN byte ranges with zero semantic guessing -- likely the highest-leverage single mechanical step available right now.

frontiers.target: First matching-C promotions inside game code (not just linked library)
frontiers.matches: Census spot-checks flagged candidates: F_A460 (9 bytes, IN AX,DX)/F_A469 (11 bytes, IN AL,DX + XOR AH,AH) look like Turbo C++ 1.00's inport()/inportb(); F_850A (12 bytes) wraps INT 21h AH=9; F_04FC/F_088E repeat 'imul dx' idioms suggesting struct-array indexing.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: None compiled/OMF-bound/byte-compared yet -- disassembly-pattern guesses only.
frontiers.unblock: Build a reusable candidate.c -> TCC 1.00 -> OBJ -> OMF extraction -> fixup binding -> full-extent byte comparison tool (generalizing tools/recover_startup_binding.py's proof standard), then run the smallest/cleanest candidates through it first.
frontiers.leverage: Establishes the first true matching-C proof loop for original game code, the central deliverable of this whole project phase.

frontiers.matches: Offset table observed at file start; 128-byte stride after the first entry is consistent with 16x16x4bpp EGA planar tiles. Not yet decoded or round-tripped.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: No chunk has been decoded, rendered, or re-encoded yet.
frontiers.unblock: Parse the offset table, decode resources under the planar-tile hypothesis, verify visually/structurally, then build an encoder and prove an exact round-trip (EGADAVE.DAV -> structured -> re-encoded EGADAVE.DAV, byte-identical) before pursuing prettier tooling. Independent of the executable-side matching-C work.
frontiers.leverage: Unlocks the entire asset/data reconstruction track in parallel with code matching.

frontiers.matches: The acquired Turbo C++ 1.0 disk set only included TASM2MSG.EXE, not TASM.EXE.
frontiers.unblock: Acquire only once a concrete hand-written-ASM extent is identified that specifically requires it; do not block matching-C work on this.
frontiers.leverage: Only relevant to MATCHING_ASM promotion, which has no identified candidates yet.

frontiers.matches: Only the unpack direction is proven; LZEXE's own compressor heuristics are not reimplemented.
frontiers.unblock: Revisit after matching-C/ASM/data work has substantially reduced RAW_UNKNOWN; the unpacked image remains the working oracle until then.
frontiers.leverage: Only closes the final packed-file-identity gap (docs/build-reconstruction.md Level 2); does not affect current matching-C progress.

frontiers.matches: Fixed-placement ownership (layout/manifest.json) remains the proof scaffold, per docs/build-reconstruction.md's four-level ladder.
frontiers.unblock: Reconstruct progressively once enough matching-C/ASM components exist to infer real module/segment ordering; do not wait for this before matching individual components.
frontiers.leverage: Needed only for 'structural build' / 'emergent whole build' levels, not for continuing placement/component-level matching now.

frontiers.target: Confirm exact Dangerous Dave release/episode variant
frontiers.matches: String extraction confirms 1990 Softdisk Dangerous Dave by John Romero; the specific episode/distribution variant (shareware vs registered) is undetermined.
frontiers.unblock: Cross-check against community fingerprint lists and in-binary level-count references when convenient; does not block any current matching-C or census work since we already have a fixed, hashed specimen.
frontiers.leverage: Low priority -- our specimen is fixed and hashed regardless of which named release it corresponds to.

end_state: Independent source modules (matching C, matching ASM, structured data/assets) compile, assemble, and link with a historically faithful toolchain such that the resulting unpacked executable image is byte-identical to the original, addresses emerge from module composition rather than being copied, and the image can subsequently be re-packed with LZEXE 0.91 to reproduce the original DAVE.EXE exactly. EGADAVE.DAV resources are simultaneously reconstructed from human-readable canonical sources (images, tables) plus deterministic encoders.
